title: Governance Dependency Graph
description: Canonical, independently identifiable and traceable structured representation of governance-significant dependency, prerequisite, ordering, authority, synchronization, consistency, execution, resource, policy, evidence, and state relationships among governed sub-transitions of a composite proposal. The graph makes dependencies explicit for composite evaluation, re-evaluation, Governance Binding Validation, Deterministic Adjudication, Partial-Bind Admissibility, Resulting-State Validation, coordinated enforcement, and replay. It does not itself establish authority, authorize execution, or determine partial-bind admissibility.
$comment: DS-036 is the authoritative Governance Dependency Graph domain object. Cross-object equality and graph-theoretic properties—including unique node identifiers, endpoint resolution, source/target inequality, cycle analysis, and correspondence with the parent proposal—require semantic validation because standard JSON Schema cannot compare arbitrary values across object locations. The schema therefore requires attributable validation assertions and integrity evidence for those properties.

nodes.description: Complete declared set of governed sub-transitions participating in the graph.

dependencies.description: Explicit governance-significant relationships among graph nodes.

governance_dependency_graph_ref.description: Stable reference to a DS-036 Governance Dependency Graph.

graph_node.description: Governed sub-transition participating in the dependency graph.

dependency_edge.description: Explicit directed or bidirectional governance-significant relationship between governed sub-transitions.

dependency_change_policy.description: Policy governing material dependency-condition changes and deterministic identification of affected nonterminal proposals.

namespaced_extensions.description: Profile-defined extensions that cannot alter the canonical dependency graph, its validation status, or its governance meaning.
